We need retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have three steps: likely disconnection at amide bond (C=O-NH), at the alkene (Doebner modification), and at sulfonamide formation.

Thus retrosynthetic steps:

1. Break amide: target -> acid (C=O) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So precursor: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1 (the acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline with NH2? The amide is C(=O)N c3ccccc3N (i.e., an aniline with an extra NH?). The amide carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl with NH2 (aniline). So the amide precursor is the acid and the aniline (with NH2). So step1: amide formation.

2. The acid precursor contains the alkene /C=C/ attached to carboxylic acid. That could be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. So break the alkene and carboxylic acid to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(=O)?) Actually the acid is attached to aromatic ring via para position: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2. The Doebner modification would give that α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid. So step2: Doebner modification.

3. The sulfonamide formation: the sulfonyl chloride reacting with an aniline. So break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl) and aniline (the first aromatic ring with methyl). So step3: sulfonamide formation.

Thus we need templates IDs for each. We can search for sulfonamide formation template (functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides). Already got some templates earlier (IDs 733 etc). Use one of them. Need to verify matching to our molecule. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching.
